clarity.justification: The method directly addresses the hypothesis by measuring the "earliest layer after which the top-1 predicted token stays fixed," comparing semantic roles and causal ablations, and then evaluating a controller using "accuracy vs mean layers executed per token (Pareto), estimated FLOPs, and wall-clock latency" against appropriate baselines. The predictions are directional—shallow roles should converge earlier, "shallow-converged tokens should tolerate late-layer removal far better than deep tokens," and the controller is expected to deliver "20-40% per-token compute savings"—so failing to show these differences or reach the savings range would refute important parts of the claim. However, "near-equal accuracy," "sufficient margin," and the exact late-layer ablation operation are not quantitatively defined, leaving the acceptable accuracy loss and part of the causal test open to interpretation.

feasibility.justification: The hardest step is the proposed partial-cache controller—"cache the partial KV ... with a fallback that recomputes skipped-layer KV lazily if a later token attends heavily"—which requires substantial custom engineering and is underspecified because detecting high attention can itself require the missing layer-specific keys; unlike activation extraction and ablation, this is not yet a standard operation as written. The named models and datasets—DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B/7B, Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B, GSM8K, MATH, and ProntoQA—exist, while logit/tuned lenses, forward hooks, residual ablation, and the stated statistical tests have established tooling support. The design includes runnable negative-result controls through full-depth decoding, uniform-confidence exit, fixed-depth truncation, lens variants, and KV-handling ablations; model scales are concretely specified as "1.5B-8B," but no token, problem, or causal-ablation sample counts are supplied, and the circular lazy-KV trigger remains a methodological roadblock requiring clarification.
